premises.statement: staging.stg_workday__organization_role exposes a role_id column in addition to organization_role_id.
premises.alternative: The staging contract lists "organization_role_id" and "organization_role_code", but no "role_id"; the same query also references "r.org_role_code" rather than the documented organization_role_code.
premises.reason: Depending on undocumented column names can prevent the entire model from executing.

premises.statement: Organization performance_category is determined solely by average employee performance rather than by a weighted composite.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: CASE WHEN avg_employee_performance_score>=80 THEN 'Excellent' WHEN avg_employee_performance_score>=60 THEN 'Good'
premises.alternative: The contract specifies "performance_category uses a weighted composite with thresholds: Excellent if composite ≥ 80; else Good if ≥ 60; else Average if ≥ 40".
premises.reason: Replacing the composite with one input can change performance categories across organizations.

premises.statement: Organization rates with zero or missing denominators may remain NULL instead of defaulting to zero.
premises.alternative: The contract specifies zero for each rate when its denominator is zero, including "annual_turnover_rate (%) ... when current_active_employees > 0, else 0".
premises.reason: NULL rates change reported values and can send health-score components and recommendations into different branches.

premises.statement: Every organization-role-worker association counted in role metrics has a matching worker assignment in that organization.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: FROM staging.stg_workday__organization_role_worker ow LEFT JOIN staging.stg_workday__organization_role r
premises.alternative: The contract requires building relationships "by left joining worker positions to role-worker and role master" before aggregating role counts.
premises.reason: Aggregating role-worker records independently includes associations that the specified assignment-based relationship would exclude.

premises.statement: Performance, career-development, retention, and age averages need not be rounded to their specified precision before being returned or used downstream.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: avg(overall_employee_score) FILTER(WHERE is_employed) avg_employee_performance_score; avg(age) FILTER(WHERE is_employed) avg_employee_age
premises.alternative: The contract requires performance, career-development, and retention averages "rounded to 2 decimals" and age "rounded to 1 decimal".
premises.reason: Unrounded averages alter output precision and can affect score rounding and threshold classifications.
